issues.overall_effect: The advertised characterization of which tubal algebras admit the Hilbert structure is not established; only a sufficient condition for a larger class is proved.
issues.title: Introduction overclaims a characterization ("these are the ones") of Hilbert-algebra tubal rings
issues.why_classification: A prose correction suffices; no formal result is affected and the proved sufficiency statement stands.

issues.failure_explanation: The Moore-Penrose conditions require (R_a R_y)^H = R_a R_y. The proof only has the ⋆_M-conjugate symmetry of a⋆y, i.e. R_{(a⋆y)*} = R_{a⋆y}; but R_{x*} = M^{-1}diag(conj(Mx))M differs from R_x^H = M^H diag(conj(Mx)) M^{-H} unless M is a scaled unitary, as the paper itself notes later. Hence R_y is in general not the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of R_a and the uniqueness argument does not apply. (The construction of y also omits the degenerate pair case γ_j = γ_k = 0.)

failure_location.quote: The same four equation hold if we replace $\va$ with $\matR_\va$, $\vy$ with $\matR_\vy$ and $\Mprod$ with matrix product. Thus, $\matR_\vy$ is the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of $\matR_\va$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the Moore-Penrose step by direct verification that M y = (M a)^+ (which follows from the definitions of δ, adding the case γ_j=γ_k=0 giving δ_j=δ_k=0), or use uniqueness of the commuting (group) inverse in a commutative von Neumann regular ring.
issues.overall_effect: The proof that a^- is real is invalid as written; the lemma's conclusion (and thus realness of the weak inverse used in Lemma lem:added-2) is unsupported by this argument, though true.
issues.title: Proof of realness of weak inverse wrongly invokes Moore-Penrose uniqueness (Hermitian conditions fail for general M)

issues.failure_explanation: The realness m ranges over {0,...,n} with the parity of n, giving ⌊n/2⌋+1 values, not ⌈n/2⌉. For n=2 the paper itself exhibits two non-isomorphic tubal rings (C, a field, and the split-complex numbers, not a field), whereas ⌈2/2⌉=1. Moreover only the 'if' direction (equal realness ⇒ isomorphic) is proved, so an exact count also needs the unproved converse.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the count by 'at most ⌊n/2⌋+1' (or prove non-isomorphism for different realness, e.g. via number of idempotents, to get exactly ⌊n/2⌋+1).
issues.overall_effect: The stated classification count of tubal rings is false for even n; Proposition prop:realness-iso itself is unaffected.
issues.title: Wrong count of tubal rings up to isomorphism
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the formula (and optionally a standard short argument for the converse) fixes the claim with no loss.

issues.failure_explanation: Elements of K_M are real. The inverse transform of Û is real only if Û_j is real whenever row j of M is real and Û_k = conj(Û_j) for conjugate row pairs (j,k). Taking arbitrary complex SVDs slice-by-slice does not guarantee this (e.g. for M=F_2 and a tube, choosing scalar SVD phases u=i in both slices yields U = M^{-1}(i,i) = (i,0), not real). The proof therefore does not produce U,V in K_M as claimed.

failure_location.quote: Construct a SVD decomposition for each frontal slices on its own, collecting the left and right unitary matrices to form \(\hat{\tenU}\) and \(\hat{\tenV}\) respectively, and the singular values in \(\hat{\tenS}\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose the slice SVDs consistently: a real SVD for slices corresponding to real rows of M, and conjugate SVD factors for conjugate row pairs; then Û, Ŝ, V̂ inverse-transform to real tensors.

issues.failure_explanation: When rows j,k of M are a conjugate pair, a real tensor X has X̂_k = conj(X̂_j). If r_j ≠ r_k the truncated slices are no longer conjugates, so the inverse transform of the defined transform-domain object is complex and [A]_r is not in K_M^{m×p}; the claimed 'optimal approximation' is not a tensor of the class being approximated, and no real tensor with such asymmetric multirank exists. The theorem imposes no symmetry condition on r (only for real M, e.g. WHT, is none needed).
